gloss: Japanese rendering of classical Chinese text (kanbun)

definitions.gloss: Japanese rendering of classical Chinese text; kanbun written in Japanese word order
definitions.explanation: A version of a classical Chinese (kanbun) text that has been rearranged into Japanese word order and supplemented with Japanese grammatical elements, making it readable as Japanese prose.

examples.japanese: ⟦{漢文|かんぶん}→漢文：13398_kanbun⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{書|か}き{下|くだ}し{文|ぶん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: To render classical Chinese into Japanese reading order.

examples.japanese: {書|か}き{下|くだ}し{文|ぶん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}んで→読む：00426_yomu⟧⟦{意味|いみ}→意味：01155_imi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{考|かんが}える→考える：00856_kangaeru⟧。
examples.english: To read the Japanese rendering and think about the meaning.

examples.japanese: ⟦{高校|こうこう}→高校：01083_koukou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{国語|こくご}→国語：02739_kokugo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{授業|じゅぎょう}→授業：00781_jugyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{漢文|かんぶん}→漢文：13398_kanbun⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{書|か}き{下|くだ}し{文|ぶん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{変換|へんかん}する→変換する：09890_henkansuru⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}→練習：05323_renshuu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: In high school Japanese class, we practiced converting kanbun into Japanese-order renderings.

notes:
A term from classical Japanese education. In kanbun study, the original Chinese text is first annotated with reading marks ({返|かえ}り{点|てん} and ⟦{送|おく}り{仮名|がな}→送り仮名：15047_okurigana⟧), then rewritten as {書|か}き{下|くだ}し{文|ぶん} — a version readable as Japanese.

KANBUN READING PROCESS:
1. {白文|はくぶん}: the original Chinese text without annotations
2. ⟦{訓読|くんどく}→訓読：18554_kundoku⟧⟦{文|ぶん}→文：03716_bun⟧: text with reading marks added
3. {書|か}き{下|くだ}し{文|ぶん}: the full Japanese-order rendering
4. {現代語訳|げんだいごやく}: modern Japanese translation

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {書|か}き{下|くだ}し{文|ぶん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to render into Japanese reading order
- {書|か}き{下|くだ}し{文|ぶん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{直|なお}す: to convert to Japanese reading order

USAGE:
This term is encountered mainly in ⟦{国語|こくご}→国語：02739_kokugo⟧ (Japanese language) education at the high school level, where students study ⟦{漢文|かんぶん}→漢文：13398_kanbun⟧ (classical Chinese texts) as part of the curriculum.
